title: The Lettermen added to the Homecoming entertainment bill
body: Dave West reported for the Herald that the Lettermen would add class to the entertainment bill for Homecoming week 1967. The issue also covered the Homecoming queen candidates and the week's schedule.
note: "West, Dave. Lettermen Add Class to Entertainment Bill" is in 47:7. But nothing ties the booking to student government, and Herald 47:5 (12 Oct) had already run "Lettermen to Perform Tuesday," pointing to a 17 October performance rather than Homecoming week.

title: The Broadway musical '1776' staged for Homecoming
body: The Herald announced that the curtain would rise on "1776" the next day, and Jeanne Jackson called it Western's best ever musical in the Homecoming issue. John Lyne's own account of his year listed the co-sponsorship of "1776" as an example of the government's move from entertainment to a wider cultural programme.
note: "Curtain Rises Tomorrow for '1776' Performance" (50:11) and "Tickets for '1776' Available Tuesday" (50:6) support a 7 October curtain. Everything tying it to student government fails: Jeanne Jackson's "best ever musical" is in neither cited index, and the 1971 Talisman contains no Lyne account of his year — only a caption, "The writing of the Declaration of Independence was portrayed through the wit and music of the cast of '1776,'" with no sponsor named.

title: Isaac Hayes plays the rescheduled date
body: The 1972 Talisman records that the concert cancelled in February was rescheduled by the Associated Students for 23 March. Stephanie Madison's review in the Herald of 28 March, "No Introductions Necessary as Isaac Hayes Movement Speaks to the People," confirms the show went ahead.
note: Madison's review "No Introductions Necessary as Isaac Hayes Movement Speaks to the People" (51:44) does show the concert went ahead. But the cited yearbook says only that Hayes "later contacted Western to reschedule his performance in March" — it does not give 23 March, and no source consulted supplies that date.

title: Jimmy Buffett plays a mini-concert
body: Jimmy Buffett came to campus on Thursday 19 April 1973 in levis and a cowboy shirt, carrying two Martin guitars, for an ASG mini-concert. The Herald had billed the show two days earlier.
note: The cited Herald 52:51, 17 Apr 1973 carries only the advance notice "Mini-Concert Set Thursday - Jimmy Buffett", which cannot support the levis, cowboy shirt, two Martin guitars, or that the show took place. All of that is in the 1973 Talisman ("On April 19, entertainer Jimmy Buffett... came to the Western campus dressed in levis and a cowboy shirt"), which is not cited. The cited headline also does not name ASG.

title: The Bar-Kays break even
body: ASG presented the Bar-Kays, the backing band on Isaac Hayes's 'Hot Buttered Soul' and 'Shaft', in one of its major mini-concerts on 25 October 1974. The seven-piece group held a distinction among campus concerts that year: ASG broke even on it.
note: The cited Herald Vol. 50 No. 17, 25 Oct 1974 carries only "Tewell, Terry. Bar-Kays to Perform in Mini-Concert Tonight" - an advance notice, which gives no financial result. The substance, including the money claim, is in the uncited 1975 Talisman: "ASG presented the Bar-Kays in one of its major mini-concerts of the year... The seven-member group held another distinction among campus concerts - ASG broke even on the Bar-Kays concert."

title: Natalie Cole sings to 325 in Van Meter
body: ASG sponsored the jazz vocalist Natalie Cole in Van Meter on 10 December 1975 before an estimated crowd of 325. The late Nat King Cole's daughter sang 'This Will Be', 'Killing Me Softly With His Song', 'Honky Tonk Women' and 'You Are the Sunshine of My Life'.
note: The cited Herald 51:29, 9 Dec 1975 carries "Associated Student Government to Sponsor Jazz Vocalist" - an advance notice the day before, which establishes ASG sponsorship but cannot give the crowd of 325 or the setlist. Those are in the uncited 1976 Talisman: "On Dec. 10, jazz vocalist Natalie Cole also performed in Van Meter to an estimated crowd of 325", with 'Killing Me Softly', 'Honky Tonk Women', 'You Are the Sunshine of My Life' and 'This Will Be'.

title: Jimmy Buffett and the Coral Reefer Band close the year
body: Jimmy Buffett and the Coral Reefer Band were set for Diddle Arena on 27 April 1977. The set drew on 'Changes in Latitudes, Changes in Attitudes', 'Livin' and Dyin' in 3/4 Time', 'A-1-A' and 'Havana Daydreamin''.
note: The cited Herald 52:47, 25 Mar 1977 carries only "Jimmy Buffett Concert Set for April 27" - an advance notice five weeks ahead, which cannot support the setlist. That is in the uncited 1977 Talisman: "Jimmy Buffett and the Coral Reefer Band appeared at Diddle Arena April 27. Highlights... included selections from 'Changes in Latitudes, Changes in Attitudes,' as well as tunes from the albums, 'Livin' and Dyin' in 3/4 Time,' 'A-1-A,' and 'Havana Daydreamin'.'" Neither source ties the show to ASG.

title: Shirley Chisholm closes the Black Awareness Symposium
body: Congresswoman Shirley Chisholm had been booked for Black Awareness Week in February but cancelled all her appearances for that month, which is why the week was stretched into a semester-long symposium. Her rescheduled free lecture filled Van Meter Auditorium at 8 p.m. on 18 April with a crowd of about 250, predominantly black, who shouted and chanted in response. She said she was a people's politician who could not be manipulated and was there "to teach and to tell people what they don't like to hear."
note: Several specifics are absent from the cited source and one is internally contradicted. Talisman 1979 pp.38-39 supports: Chisholm was rescheduled to April 18 after cancelling her February lecture, which is why Black Awareness Week became a semester-long symposium; 'The crowd of about 250, predominantly black, shouted and chanted in response'; she is 'a people's politician' who 'cannot be manipulated'; 'here to teach and to tell people what they don't like to hear.' NOT in the source: the venue (Van Meter), the 8 p.m. start, that the lecture was free, and 'filled Van Meter Auditorium' - the same yearbook states on p.79 that Van Meter 'holds slightly more than 1,000,' so 250 people cannot have filled it. Also 'cancelled all her appearances for that month' is the 18 January Herald's wording, not the Talisman's, which says only that she 'canceled her February lecture.' And as with the other lecture entries, the cited section makes no ASG connection.

title: ASG president assassinated in a members-only killing game
body: ASG members spent the autumn playing an assassination game with toy guns, and president Tim Todd was shot at about 8 p.m. on 2 October in his State Street apartment while wearing only a bathrobe, fresh out of the shower. Kathryn Michelsen, who killed Todd and three other congress members the same night, led the field in kills until Gamaliel freshman Janet Dyer shot her between the eyes near the university center. Dyer killed three more people that Sunday, two of them in front of their girlfriends.
note: Herald 62:13, 9 Oct 1986, "ASG members all wet from playing with guns." Most of the entry checks out: Tim Todd "was assassinated last Thursday at about 8 p.m. wearing only a bathrobe in his State Street apartment" (9 Oct issue, so 2 Oct - date correct); the game was ASG's, "sponsored by the Public Relations Committee"; Michelsen led in kills "until Gamaliel freshman Janet Dyer shot her" "right between the eyes" near the university center. BUT the Sunday kills are misattributed. The source: "Michelsen killed three other congress members the same night she shot Todd, including a sleeping Holger Velastegui. Sunday night SHE killed three people, two of whom were slain in front of their girlfriends." That is Michelsen, not Dyer - and Dyer did not shoot Michelsen until "last night" (Wed 8 Oct), after that Sunday. The entry's final sentence must be rewritten. Minor: the weapons are squirt/water guns, not generic "toy guns."

title: Coach for a Game puts a student on the bench with Ralph Willard
body: ASG created Coach for a Game as a spring counterpart to the fall's President for a Day, selling raffle tickets at 50 cents each with every member required to sell ten and the proceeds going to a philanthropic cause. Members sold from tables at Downing University Center and in DUC 119 from 10 a.m. to 2 p.m. on 24 and 25 February, and the draw was held at the ASG meeting on 25 February. The winner served as Coach Ralph Willard's new assistant at the men's basketball game against Central Florida on 29 February, and public relations vice president Mistianna Holcomb, who wrote the bill, said it would become an annual event.
money: raffle tickets 50 cents each, ten per member

src.label: SGA Records, Bill 92-03-S, Establishment of a Coach for a Game Program

note: REJECT - the cited document supports almost none of the entry. Bill 92-03-S (verified on the page image) is UNDATED: the "INTRODUCED:" line is blank and First Reading, Second Reading, Pass, Fail and Other are all blank, so it cannot support a 1992-02-29 date or any date. It contains only: the purpose "To establish a Coach for a Game program"; "In the fall, ASG does sponsor President for a Day"; "it should be mandatory for each ASG member to sell ten tickets for this project at $.50 per ticket"; "The proceeds from this event will go towards a philanthropic cause"; AUTHOR: Mistianna Holcomb; SPONSOR: Public Relations. It says NOTHING about Ralph Willard, the Central Florida game, 29 February, the DUC and DUC 119 ticket tables on 24-25 February, the 10 a.m.-2 p.m. hours, the 25 February drawing, Holcomb's job title, or her saying it would become annual. Those all need a separate citation (minutes or a Herald story) or must be cut.

title: $2,250 of organizational aid split between thirteen groups
body: Bill 94-2-S disbursed the $2,250 budgeted for organizational aid, after the committee spent more than four hours across three meetings deciding between applicants. Alpha Phi Omega, Campus Crusade for Christ and Delta Sigma Theta took $250 each, Beta Alpha Psi $200, the Topperettes $350, and the Association of Resident Assistants, Fellowship of Christian Athletes, International Club, Legion of Veterans, Phi Beta Sigma, SOTA, Students' Right to Life and United Student Activists shared the rest in grants of $100 to $150. It passed on 8 March 1994.

src.label: SGA Records, Bill 94-2-S, Organizational Aid Recipients

note: Bill 94-2-S. The frame is right - "First Reading 03-01-94 / Second Reading 03-08-94" stamped PASSED; "INTRODUCED: March 1, 1994"; "to disperse the $2,250.00 budgeted for Organizational Aid"; "The Organizational Aid Committee has spent over four hours in three meetings"; thirteen recipients. BUT TWO AMOUNTS ARE SWAPPED. I read the bill as a page image to be certain. The schedule is: Alpha Phi Omega $250, Association of Resident Assistants $125, Beta Alpha Psi $200, Campus Crusade for Christ $250, Delta Sigma Theta Sorority $250, Fellowship of Christian Athletes $150, International Club $100, Legion of Veterans Association $125, PHI BETA SIGMA FRATERNITY $350, S.O.T.A. $100, Students' Right to Life $125, TOPPERETTES $100, United Student Activists $125 (sums to $2,250). The entry gives the Topperettes $350 and buries Phi Beta Sigma in the $100-$150 group; it is the other way round. Also, the residual group's range is $100-$150 only if Phi Beta Sigma is excluded, which the corrected reading allows.

title: President for a Day puts a student in Wetherby
body: SGA's President for a Day swap put student Nick Church in President Thomas Meredith's job for a day. The Herald carried paired pieces from Meredith and Church under the heading "Back to the ABCz."

src.label: Herald 70:35, 28 Feb 1995 - Grundy and Gagliardi, "Back to the ABCz - President for a Day"

note: The two articles exist ('Grundy, Julie. Back to the ABCz - President for a Day, Thomas Meredith' and 'Gagliardi, Melissa. Back to the ABCz - President for a Day, Nick Church', 28 Feb 1995), but neither is tied to student government. This archive tags SGA items explicitly - the clean-up item in the very same issue reads '- Student Government Association' - and these two carry no such tag. Nothing in the source calls it an SGA programme or mentions Wetherby.

title: Dialogue Day at Java City
body: SGA ran Dialogue Day on Tuesday 28 October 2003 from 12 to 2 p.m. at Java City near the library, giving students a chance to meet WKU administrators including their deans. It became a fixture SGA repeated in later years.

src.label: WKU SGA news page, 26 Oct 2003 (Wayback capture)

note: The cited page is a pre-event announcement, not a record of an event. Its 26 October 2003 item reads: 'Dialogue Day on Tuesday! Get a chance to meet WKU administrators, including your deans! It's on Tuesday at Java City (near the library) from 12:00 to 2:00.' The venue, hours and purpose all match, but nothing in the source shows the event took place, and 'It became a fixture SGA repeated in later years' is unsupported by this capture.

title: Safety Walk found nearly thirty lights out
body: SGA held its annual Safety Walk on the evening of 26 October 2010, with Assistant Police Chief Mike Wallace and John Osborne, vice president for campus services and facilities, taking part. Executive vice president Kendrick Bryan reported that participants had found nearly 30 lights out around campus.

src.label: Herald, 10 Nov 2010 - "SGA invites regents to Dine with Decision Makers"

note: The cited 10 Nov 2010 article supports only the lights figure: 'Bryan said participants found nearly 30 lights that were out on campus at last week's campus safety walk.' It gives NO date - and 'last week's' relative to 10 November points to roughly 1-7 November, not 26 October. It also does not mention Mike Wallace or John Osborne at all. Those two names and the 26 October date come from the 19 Oct SGA-notes article, which said the walk 'will take place next Tuesday at 6 p.m.' with Wallace and Osborne 'helping out' - i.e. scheduled, not confirmed as attended. The entry needs re-sourcing or a corrected date.
